history.dynasty: Vijayanagara-era roots; relocated under Portuguese persecution; Mahajans of Margao
history.summary: The deity was originally enshrined in a large temple at Mathagram (Madgaon/Margao), where the Holy Spirit Church now stands. After the Portuguese temple-destruction campaign in Sasashti taluka (1565-1567; Diogo Rodrigues burnt Margao's temples and a church was raised on the Damodar temple's ruins in 1565), the Mahajans of Margao shifted the deities - Ramnath, Damodar, Laxmi-Narayan, Chamundeshwari, Mahakali, Mahesh - to Zambaulim, with land donated by the Desais of Rivona (Vatan still paid). Records of the original Zambaulim construction are unavailable; the present large temple replaced a small one in 1910. Folk tradition holds the temple was consecrated to the memory of Makaji Damodar of Margao. The Mahajans are the Prabhudesais of the Goud Saraswat community. Note: sources conflict on the deity's nature - described both as a form of Vishnu/Krishna and as 'Shiva incarnated as Damodar'; recorded here as documented without resolution. CSV town correction: the temple is at Zambaulim (Molcornem), Quepem taluka, South Goa - NOT Vasco da Gama as the CSV claims. Coordinates are approximate (street-level geocode; no POI match).

name: Shree Damodar Temple
town_description: Zambaulim (in Molcornem) is a village in Quepem taluka, South Goa, on the banks of the Kushavati river, about 22 km from Margao and 5 km from Quepem. It was the inland refuge where Margao's Mahajans relocated their deities in the 1560s to escape Portuguese persecution.
